docs.title: specpls
docs.text:
PLS calibration models for process spectroscopy (Raman, NIR) in bioprocessing.

specpls packages a standard chemometrics workflow as a tested Python library:

  1. Load spectra and reference values from CSV or MATLAB files.
  2. Preprocess with SNV, MSC, Savitzky-Golay, baseline correction and region selection.
  3. Calibrate a PLS model, choosing the number of latent variables by cross-validation (including leave-one-batch-out).
  4. Diagnose with RMSEC / RMSECV / RMSEP, VIP, Hotelling's T² and Q residuals.
  5. Deploy with versioned model files, axis checks and a command-line tool.
from specpls import PLSModel
from specpls.datasets import make_synthetic_cell_culture

data = make_synthetic_cell_culture(random_state=0)
model = PLSModel(preprocessing="savgol:11:2:1", cv="batch").fit(
    data.X, data.target("glucose"), groups=data.meta["batch"], target_name="glucose"
)
print(model.summary())

Start with Getting started, or see the API reference.

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
Bases: RegressorMixin, BaseEstimator

Single-response PLS calibration for spectroscopic data.

Wraps preprocessing and :class:sklearn.cross_decomposition.PLSRegression in one scikit-learn estimator and adds what a chemometric workflow needs: automatic choice of latent variables from RMSECV, Hotelling's T2 and Q-residual diagnostics, VIP scores, and safe save/load for deployment.

Preprocessing is fitted inside every cross-validation fold, so RMSECV is not optimistically biased by data-dependent steps such as MSC.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default preprocessing str, list of transformers, Pipeline or None

Preprocessing applied before PLS. A string such as "savgol:15:2:1,snv" is parsed with :func:specpls.preprocessing.build_preprocessing.

None n_components int or 'auto'

Number of latent variables. "auto" picks it from RMSECV using lv_rule.

"auto" max_components int

Largest number of LVs tried when n_components="auto".

10 cv (int, str or splitter)

Cross-validation scheme, see :func:specpls.validation.make_cv. Use "batch" together with groups in :meth:fit to hold out whole bioreactor runs.

10 lv_rule ('parsimonious', 'min', 'first_min')

Rule for choosing LVs from the RMSECV curve.

"parsimonious" lv_tolerance float

Relative tolerance for the parsimonious rule.

0.02 regions list of (low, high)

Wavenumber regions to keep, e.g. [(400, 1800)]. Applied before preprocessing. Requires wavenumbers in :meth:fit.

None scale bool

Autoscale variables inside PLS. Spectra are normally only mean-centred, so the default is False (unlike scikit-learn).

False max_cv_ratio float

Over-fitting guard for automatic LV selection: only LVs with RMSECV / RMSEC <= max_cv_ratio are eligible (1.2 = RMSECV at most 20 % above RMSEC). A warning is issued if no LV qualifies.

None

Attributes:

Name Type Description n_components_ int

Number of LVs in the final model.

rmsecv_curve_ ndarray

RMSECV for 1..max_components LVs (None if LVs were fixed).

rmsec_curve_ ndarray

RMSEC for the same LVs (None if LVs were fixed).

ratio_ok_ bool

False if max_cv_ratio was set and no LV satisfied it.

cv_predictions_ ndarray

Cross-validated predictions for the training samples.

pipeline_ Pipeline

The fitted region selection + preprocessing + PLS pipeline.

calibration_ dict

Figures of merit for calibration (RMSEC) and cross-validation (RMSECV).

wavenumbers_ ndarray or None

Wavenumber axis the model was trained on.

target_name_ str or None

Name of the predicted variable, e.g. "glucose".

Examples:

>>> from specpls import PLSModel
>>> from specpls.datasets import make_synthetic_cell_culture
>>> data = make_synthetic_cell_culture(random_state=0)
>>> model = PLSModel(preprocessing="savgol:15:2:1,snv", max_components=8)
>>> model = model.fit(data.X, data.target("glucose"),
...                   wavenumbers=data.wavenumbers, target_name="glucose")
>>> model.n_components_ > 0
True

Load a model saved with :meth:PLSModel.save.

Warns if it was created with a different scikit-learn version, because pickled estimators are not guaranteed to be compatible across versions.

Only load files from sources you trust: joblib files can execute code.

Predict the response for new spectra.

If wavenumbers is given, it is checked against the calibration axis, which guards against applying a model to spectra from a different instrument set-up.

One-row summary in the style of a publication table.

docs.title: t2_limit(confidence=0.95)
docs.text:
T2 control limit based on the F distribution.

A (n-1) / (n-A) * F(confidence; A, n-A) with A LVs and n calibration samples.

docs.title: q_limit(confidence=0.95)
docs.text: Q control limit using Box's scaled chi-square approximation.

docs.title: outliers(X, confidence=0.95)
docs.text: T2, Q and boolean flags for samples outside the control limits.

docs.title: vip()
docs.text:
Variable Importance in Projection for each (selected) wavenumber.

Variables with VIP > 1 are conventionally considered important. The mean of VIP**2 over all variables equals 1.

docs.title: Preprocessing
docs.text:
Spectral preprocessing transformers.

Every transformer follows the scikit-learn fit/transform API, so they can be chained in a :class:sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline and are re-fitted inside each cross-validation fold. That matters for data-dependent methods such as MSC, whose reference spectrum must come from the training data only.

Spectra are always arranged as (n_samples, n_wavenumbers).
Short names accepted by :func:build_preprocessing and the CLI.

docs.title: SNV
docs.text:
Bases: _SpectralTransformer

Standard Normal Variate: centre and scale each spectrum individually.

Removes multiplicative scatter and path-length effects. Stateless: fitting only records the number of wavenumbers.

docs.title: MSC
docs.text:
Bases: _SpectralTransformer

Multiplicative Scatter Correction.

Each spectrum x is regressed on a reference spectrum r (x = a + b * r) and corrected as (x - a) / b.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default reference array-like of shape (n_wavenumbers,)

Fixed reference spectrum. If None (default), the mean spectrum of the training data is used.

None

docs.title: SavitzkyGolay
docs.text:
Bases: _SpectralTransformer

Savitzky-Golay smoothing or derivative along the wavenumber axis.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default window_length int

Number of points in the filter window. Must be odd and greater than polyorder.

15 polyorder int

Order of the fitted polynomial.

2 deriv int

Derivative order (0 = smoothing only, 1 = first derivative, ...).

0

docs.title: Detrend
docs.text:
Bases: _SpectralTransformer

Subtract a low-order polynomial baseline fitted to each spectrum.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default order int

Polynomial order (0 = offset, 1 = linear, 2 = quadratic, ...).

1

docs.title: AsLSBaseline
docs.text:
Bases: _SpectralTransformer

Asymmetric Least Squares baseline removal (Eilers & Boelens, 2005).

Fits a smooth baseline that stays below the Raman peaks, which suits broad fluorescence backgrounds.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default lam float

Smoothness penalty. Larger values give a stiffer baseline.

1e5 p float

Asymmetry weight for points above the baseline (0 < p < 1).

0.01 n_iter int

Number of reweighting iterations.

10

docs.title: RegionSelector
docs.text:
Bases: _SpectralTransformer

Keep only selected wavenumber regions.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default wavenumbers array-like of shape (n_wavenumbers,)

Wavenumber axis of the incoming spectra (e.g. Raman shift in cm-1).

None regions sequence of (low, high) tuples

Inclusive ranges to keep, e.g. [(400, 1800)] or [(800, 1200), (1400, 1500)].

None

docs.title: EPO
docs.text:
Bases: _SpectralTransformer

External Parameter Orthogonalisation (Roger et al., 2003).

Estimates the directions of unwanted spectral variation ("clutter") and projects every spectrum onto the space orthogonal to them: X_epo = X (I - V V'), where V holds the first n_components right singular vectors of the clutter matrix D.

How D is built:

  • clutter given: those spectra are used as D directly, e.g. differences between the same sample measured at two temperatures or in two vessels.
  • otherwise (default, "y-gradient", as in PLS_Toolbox GLSW/EPO): the calibration spectra are sorted by y and D contains differences between neighbouring samples. Samples with nearly the same analyte concentration should have nearly the same spectrum, so what differs between them is interference (fluorescence, cell density, matrix).

y is required in fit for the y-gradient mode. Inside :class:~specpls.model.PLSModel it is fitted on the training folds only.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default n_components int

Number of clutter directions removed. Choose by RMSECV; too many removes analyte signal.

2 clutter array-like of shape (n_clutter, n_wavenumbers)

Explicit clutter (difference) spectra, already preprocessed the same way as X.

None

docs.title: VariableSelector
docs.text:
Bases: _SpectralTransformer

Keep a fixed subset of variables (e.g. intervals chosen by iPLS).

Unlike :class:RegionSelector it works on column positions, so it can be placed after preprocessing.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mask array-like of bool or int

Boolean mask over the variables, or integer column indices.

None

docs.title: build_preprocessing(spec)
docs.text:
Build a preprocessing pipeline from a compact text specification.

Steps are separated by commas and arguments by colons, applied in order.

Examples:

>>> build_preprocessing("savgol:15:2:1,snv")   # 1st derivative, then SNV
Pipeline(steps=[('savitzkygolay', SavitzkyGolay(deriv=1)), ('snv', SNV())])

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default spec str, list of transformers, or None

A string such as "asls:1e5:0.01,snv", a list of already-built transformers, or None/"" for no preprocessing.

required

Returns:

Type Description Pipeline or None

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Figures of merit and cross-validation schemes for calibration models.

docs.title: VenetianBlinds
docs.text:
Bases: BaseCrossValidator

Venetian-blinds cross-validation (sample i goes to fold i % k).

This is the default scheme in many chemometrics packages (e.g. "vet" in PLS_Toolbox). It assumes samples are ordered, e.g. by time or concentration, so that every fold spans the whole range.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default n_splits int

Number of folds.

10

docs.title: LVSelection dataclass
docs.text:
Result of latent-variable selection.

ratio_ok is False when a max_ratio was requested but no number of LVs satisfied it; the LV count with the smallest RMSECV/RMSEC ratio is returned in that case.

docs.title: rmse(y_true, y_pred)
docs.text: Root mean square error. Used for RMSEC, RMSECV and RMSEP.

docs.title: r2(y_true, y_pred)
docs.text: Coefficient of determination, 1 - SS_res / SS_tot.

docs.title: bias(y_true, y_pred)
docs.text: Mean of y_pred - y_true. Positive means the model over-predicts.

docs.title: sep(y_true, y_pred)
docs.text:
Standard error of prediction, corrected for bias.

RMSEP**2 ~= SEP**2 + bias**2 (exact up to the n / n-1 factor).

docs.title: rpd(y_true, y_pred)
docs.text: Ratio of performance to deviation: SD(y_true) / SEP.

docs.title: regression_metrics(y_true, y_pred)
docs.text: All figures of merit as a dict: rmse, r2, bias, sep, rpd, n.

docs.title: make_cv(cv=10, groups=None)
docs.text:
Turn a short description into a scikit-learn CV splitter.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default cv (int, str or splitter)
  • int - venetian blinds with that many folds
  • "venetian:k" - venetian blinds, k folds
  • "kfold:k" - contiguous blocks, k folds (no shuffling)
  • "loo" - leave-one-out
  • "batch" / "group" - leave-one-group-out; requires groups. Use this for bioprocess data so that all samples from one batch or bioreactor run are held out together.
  • any object with a split method is returned unchanged.
10 groups array - like

Group labels (e.g. batch IDs). Required for "batch".

None

docs.title: select_n_components(rmsecv, rule='parsimonious', tolerance=0.02, rmsec=None, max_ratio=None)
docs.text:
Pick the number of latent variables from an RMSECV curve.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rmsecv array - like

RMSECV for 1, 2, ..., A latent variables.

required rule ('parsimonious', 'min', 'first_min')
  • "min" - global minimum. Tends to over-fit on small data sets.
  • "first_min" - first local minimum of the curve.
  • "parsimonious" (default) - fewest LVs whose RMSECV is within tolerance (relative) of the global minimum. Trades a negligible loss of accuracy for a simpler, more robust model.
"parsimonious" tolerance float

Relative tolerance for the parsimonious rule (0.02 = 2 %).

0.02 rmsec array - like

RMSEC for the same LVs. Required with max_ratio.

None max_ratio float

Over-fitting guard: only LVs with RMSECV / RMSEC <= max_ratio are eligible (e.g. 1.2 means RMSECV may exceed RMSEC by at most 20 %). The rule is then applied among the eligible LVs.

None

Returns:

Type Description LVSelection

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
Loading spectra and reference values from CSV, Excel-exported CSV and MATLAB files.

Synthetic Raman-like cell-culture data for examples, tests and teaching.

The data are simulated. They mimic the structure of CHO fed-batch Raman data (glucose and lactate bands, cell-related bands, a broad fluorescence background that grows with cell density, scatter and noise) so the package can be demonstrated without sharing proprietary spectra.

Spectral axis (e.g. Raman shift in cm-1).

meta DataFrame

One row per sample: reference values (glucose, lactate, ...), batch IDs, culture day, etc.

docs.title: Plotting
docs.text:
Standard diagnostic plots for a fitted :class:~specpls.model.PLSModel.

Requires matplotlib (pip install "specpls[plot]"). Every function accepts an optional ax and returns the axes, so plots can be combined in figures.

docs.title: plot_spectra(wavenumbers, X, color_by=None, ax=None, cmap='viridis', label=None)
docs.text: Overlay spectra, optionally coloured by a reference value.

docs.title: plot_rmsecv(model, ax=None)
docs.text: RMSECV versus number of latent variables, with the chosen LV marked.

docs.title: plot_predicted_vs_measured(model, y_cal, X_test=None, y_test=None, ax=None, units='')
docs.text: Cross-validated (and optional test-set) predictions against reference.

docs.title: plot_vip(model, ax=None, threshold=1.0)
docs.text: VIP scores across the spectrum with the VIP = 1 threshold.

docs.title: plot_t2_q(model, X, ax=None, confidence=0.95, labels=None, X_test=None, test_labels=None)
docs.text:
Hotelling's T2 versus Q residuals with control limits.

X is plotted as calibration (blue circles); an optional X_test is added as test samples (orange diamonds). Samples outside a limit are labelled when labels are given.

docs.title: plot_scores(model, X, y=None, X_test=None, y_test=None, components=(1, 2), ax=None)
docs.text:
Score plot.

With two or more LVs: LV components[0] versus LV components[1]. With a one-LV model: LV1 score for each sample (sample order on x). Points are calibration (blue circles) and test (orange diamonds).

docs.title: plot_loadings(model, components=None, ax=None)
docs.text: X-loadings of the selected LVs across the spectrum.

docs.title: plot_overview(model, X_cal, y_cal, X_test=None, y_test=None, units='')
docs.text: Four-panel figure: RMSECV, predicted vs measured, VIP, T2-Q.

docs.title: plot_ipls(result, X=None, ax=None)
docs.text:
Classic iPLS plot: RMSECV of each interval, selected intervals highlighted.

The dashed line is the all-variable model; the grey curve (if X is given) is the mean spectrum for orientation.

docs.title: Saving models
docs.text:
model.save("models/glucose_v1.joblib")

The file contains the fitted pipeline (region selection, preprocessing, PLS), the calibration wavenumber axis, the control-limit statistics and metadata: specpls version, scikit-learn version and creation time.

load_model warns if the scikit-learn version differs from the one used for saving, because pickled estimators are not guaranteed to be compatible across versions. Re-validate the model in that case.

Only load trusted files

joblib/pickle files can execute code when loaded. Load model files only from sources you trust.

docs.title: Guarding predictions
docs.text:
model.predict(X_new, wavenumbers=new_axis)

Passing the wavenumber axis makes the model refuse spectra recorded on a different axis (for example after an instrument or software change) instead of silently returning wrong numbers. Combine with model.outliers() to flag spectra outside the calibration space.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
specpls train calibration.csv --target glucose --preprocess "savgol:15:2:1,snv" \
    --region 400:1800 --cv batch --groups batch --test-col is_test --out glucose.joblib

specpls predict glucose.joblib new.csv --id-col sample_id --out predictions.csv

train prints the summary table as JSON. predict writes predictions, T², Q and an outside_limits column.

docs.title: Developer guide
docs.text: How the project is engineered, and how to work on it.

docs.title: Design principles
docs.text:
• scikit-learn compatible. Every transformer and the model implement fit / transform / predict and get_params, so they work with Pipeline, clone, GridSearchCV and other tools.
  • No leakage by construction. Preprocessing is part of the model and is re-fitted in each CV fold.
  • Fail loudly. Wrong shapes, mismatched wavenumber axes, NaNs in the reference values and invalid parameters raise clear errors.
  • Small modules with one job (preprocessing, validation, model, io, plotting, cli). Plotting is optional so servers can install without matplotlib.

docs.title: Tooling
docs.text: Tool Purpose Command git + GitHub Version control, pull requests, review git switch -c feat/... pytest Unit, reference and integration tests; doctests pytest pytest-cov Coverage pytest --cov ruff Linting and formatting ruff check . && ruff format . pre-commit Runs ruff before every commit pre-commit install GitHub Actions CI on Linux/Windows, Python 3.10–3.13, docs build automatic MkDocs + mkdocstrings This site, API docs generated from docstrings mkdocs serve

docs.title: Test strategy
docs.text: Kind Example Known answer SNV of 3·x + 5 equals SNV of x; MSC recovers the reference Reference implementation PLSModel predictions equal an independent SIMPLS and plain scikit-learn Property Mean VIP² = 1; mean calibration T² = A(n-1)/n; CV tests each sample once Behaviour A spectrum with an unseen spike is flagged by Q Error handling Wrong widths, unknown preprocessing names, bad CV specs Integration CLI train → predict round trip; example scripts run

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: See CONTRIBUTING.md for branches, commit messages, pull requests and the review checklist.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
• Locally weighted PLS (LW-PLS) for nonlinear and drifting processes
  • Interval PLS / VIP-based variable selection
  • Model transfer (piecewise direct standardisation) between instruments
  • Multi-response (PLS2) support

docs.title: VIP scores
docs.text:
vip = model.vip()  # one value per wavenumber in the model
important = model.model_wavenumbers_[vip > 1]

Variable Importance in Projection summarises how much each wavenumber contributes to the explained variance of the response. The mean of VIP² is 1, so VIP > 1 marks above-average importance. Check that important regions match known bands of the analyte (for glucose, around 1060–1130 cm⁻¹) rather than background.

docs.title: Hotelling's T² and Q residuals
docs.text:
flags = model.outliers(X_new, confidence=0.95)
flags["t2"], flags["q"]  # per-sample statistics
flags["t2_limit"], flags["q_limit"]  # control limits
flags["t2_flag"] | flags["q_flag"]  # samples to investigate
  • T²: distance from the model centre within the LV space. High T² means an unusual but model-consistent sample (e.g. an extreme concentration).
  • Q: squared residual outside the LV space. High Q means the spectrum contains variation the model has not seen (new component, fluorescence change, probe fouling). Predictions for these samples should not be trusted.

Limits:

  • T²: A (n-1)/(n-A) · F(α; A, n-A)
  • Q: Box's scaled χ² approximation from the calibration residuals.

docs.title: Plots
docs.text:
from specpls.plotting import plot_t2_q, plot_vip, plot_overview

plot_t2_q(model, X_new, labels=sample_ids)

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install "specpls[plot] @ git+https://github.com/mahdishaikat/specpls"

Python 3.10 or newer is required. The plot extra installs matplotlib.

docs.title: Prepare your data
docs.text:
specpls reads a wide table: one row per spectrum, metadata columns first, then one column per wavenumber. Any column whose header is a number is treated as a wavenumber.

sample_id batch day glucose lactate 400 401 ... 1800 R1-D00 R1 0 5.78 0.07 812.1 815.4 ... 402.3 R1-D01 R1 1 5.21 0.45 820.7 822.0 ... 410.9 
from specpls import load_csv

data = load_csv("calibration.csv")
data.X  # (n_samples, n_wavenumbers) array
data.wavenumbers  # (n_wavenumbers,) array
data.meta  # pandas DataFrame with sample_id, batch, glucose, ...

Coming from MATLAB? Save with save('spectra.mat', 'X', 'wavenumbers', 'glucose', 'batch', '-v7') and load with load_mat("spectra.mat", meta_keys=["glucose", "batch"]).

docs.title: Fit a model
docs.text:
from specpls import PLSModel

is_test = (data.meta["batch"] == "R6").to_numpy()  # hold out a whole run
cal, test = data.subset(~is_test), data.subset(is_test)

model = PLSModel(
    preprocessing="savgol:15:2:1,snv",
    regions=[(400, 1800)],
    max_components=10,
    cv="batch",
)
model.fit(
    cal.X,
    cal.target("glucose"),
    wavenumbers=cal.wavenumbers,
    groups=cal.meta["batch"],
    target_name="glucose",
)

model.summary(test.X, test.target("glucose"))

docs.title: Plot
docs.text:
from specpls.plotting import plot_overview

fig = plot_overview(
    model, cal.X, cal.target("glucose"), test.X, test.target("glucose"), units="g/L"
)
fig.savefig("glucose.png", dpi=150)

docs.title: Save and reuse
docs.text:
model.save("glucose.joblib")

from specpls import load_model

model = load_model("glucose.joblib")
model.predict(new_spectra, wavenumbers=new_axis)

docs.title: Choosing the number of latent variables
docs.text:
With n_components="auto" (the default), the model is cross-validated for 1 to max_components LVs and one is chosen from the RMSECV curve:

lv_rule Picks "parsimonious" (default) Fewest LVs with RMSECV within lv_tolerance (2 %) of the minimum "min" Global minimum of RMSECV "first_min" First local minimum

"min" often adds LVs that improve RMSECV by a negligible amount and make the model less robust. Set n_components=5 to fix the number instead.

The full curve is in model.rmsecv_curve_ and can be plotted with specpls.plotting.plot_rmsecv(model).

docs.title: Cross-validation schemes
docs.text:
cv= Scheme When to use 10 or "venetian:10" Venetian blinds Samples ordered by time or concentration "kfold:5" Contiguous blocks Checking extrapolation along the sample order "loo" Leave-one-out Very small data sets "batch" + groups= Leave-one-batch-out Bioprocess data: samples from the same run are correlated

Use leave-one-batch-out for bioreactor data

Daily samples from the same run share media, cells and fluorescence background. Random or venetian CV puts samples from the same run in both training and validation, which makes RMSECV look better than performance on a new run will be.

docs.title: Figures of merit
docs.text:
model.calibration_  # rmsec, r2_cal, rmsecv, r2_cv
model.evaluate(X_test, y_test)  # rmsep, r2, bias, sep, rpd, n
model.summary(X_test, y_test)  # one row for a results table
  • RMSEC: error on the calibration samples (always optimistic).
  • RMSECV: cross-validation error, used for model selection.
  • RMSEP: error on an independent test set, for the final performance claim.
  • SEP and bias split RMSEP into random and systematic error.
  • RPD: SD of reference values / SEP.

docs.title: Algorithm
docs.text: PLSModel uses scikit-learn's NIPALS PLSRegression with mean-centring only (scale=False). For a single response this gives the same model as SIMPLS (MATLAB plsregress, PLS_Toolbox); the test suite checks this against an independent SIMPLS implementation.

docs.title: Preprocessing
docs.text:
All preprocessing steps are scikit-learn transformers. Pass them to PLSModel(preprocessing=...) as a short string, a list, or a Pipeline.

Name in string Class Purpose Arguments snv SNV Per-spectrum centring and scaling; removes multiplicative scatter none msc MSC Regress each spectrum on a reference (training mean) none savgol / sg SavitzkyGolay Smoothing or derivatives window, polyorder, deriv detrend Detrend Subtract a polynomial baseline order asls AsLSBaseline Asymmetric least-squares baseline, good for fluorescence lam, p, n_iter epo EPO External Parameter Orthogonalisation: removes interference directions estimated from samples with similar y (or from given clutter spectra) n_components

Steps are applied left to right:

PLSModel(preprocessing="savgol:15:2:1,snv")  # SG 1st derivative, then SNV
PLSModel(preprocessing="asls:1e5:0.01,savgol:11:2:0")  # baseline, then smooth

or with objects:

from specpls import SNV, SavitzkyGolay

PLSModel(preprocessing=[SavitzkyGolay(15, 2, 1), SNV()])

docs.title: Region selection
docs.text:
Use regions on the model rather than slicing arrays by hand, so the selection is stored with the model and applied automatically at prediction:

PLSModel(regions=[(400, 1800)])  # fingerprint region
PLSModel(regions=[(800, 1200), (1400, 1500)])  # several windows

Why preprocessing lives inside the model

Data-dependent steps (MSC's reference spectrum, for example) are fitted on the training folds only during cross-validation. Preprocessing the whole data set first and then cross-validating leaks information from the validation samples and gives an optimistic RMSECV.

docs.title: Choosing preprocessing
docs.text:
Compare candidates on RMSECV, and keep the test set for a final check:

python examples/02_compare_preprocessing.py

docs.title: Interval PLS (iPLS)
docs.text:
Forward iPLS splits the (preprocessed) spectrum into intervals and adds the interval that lowers RMSECV most, one at a time:

from specpls import ipls, PLSModel, SNV, SavitzkyGolay, EPO, VariableSelector

result = ipls(
    X,
    y,
    preprocessing="snv,savgol:21:2:0,epo:4",
    n_intervals=20,
    max_intervals=4,
    cv=10,
    wavenumbers=axis,
)
print(result.summary())

model = PLSModel(
    preprocessing=[SNV(), SavitzkyGolay(21, 2, 0), EPO(4), VariableSelector(result.mask)],
    n_components=result.n_components,
).fit(X, y, wavenumbers=axis)

Selection bias

The RMSECV reported by iPLS is optimistic because the same cross-validation picks the intervals. Always confirm on an independent test set.
